design_detail: Retrospective pharmacokinetic analysis of two laboratory phases in 14 men with recreational MDMA experience, none of which was designed to test dose proportionality (Discussion, 3rd paragraph). Pilot phase: six men took one oral dose of racemic MDMA, two each at 50, 100 and 150 mg. Second phase: eight men in a double-blind, randomized, balanced 4 x 4 Latin-square crossover took 75 mg MDMA, 125 mg MDMA, 40 mg amphetamine and placebo, so the 75 and 125 mg comparison is within person (n=8). Plasma MDMA, MDA, HMMA and HMA were measured at 13 times to 24 hours and urine over 0-24 hours, and the analysis compares dose-normalized exposure, clearance and urinary recovery across dose levels. Plasma HMMA was re-measured in five men, one per dose level, and blood pressure at the time of peak concentration is plotted for the same five.
can_establish: Whether, in eight men who are extensive CYP2D6 metabolizers, 125 mg of MDMA gives a peak concentration and exposure that rise by more than the 1.67-fold increase in dose from 75 mg, with a fall in non-renal clearance, and what the urinary metabolite pattern looks like across five doses.
cannot_establish: A dose-response curve between 50 and 150 mg (three of the five doses rest on two men each, different men at each dose); whether the same holds in women, in people who metabolize MDMA slowly or at intermediate speed, or at repeated or recreational dose patterns; whether the cause is saturation or self-inhibition of CYP2D6, which no measurement here separates; or anything about toxicity, which was not analysed.

sample.recruitment: Men recruited by word of mouth and interviewed; the protocol was approved by an institutional ethics committee and authorized by the Spanish Ministry of Health, which also supplied the MDMA; volunteers gave written consent and were paid (Methods > Patients and study design, 1st and 2nd paragraphs).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Recreational MDMA use on at least five occasions; interview to exclude other conditions; major psychiatric disorder (structured clinical interview for DSM-IV) excluded; physical examination, blood and urine tests and 12-lead electrocardiogram; no history of drug abuse or dependence by DSM-IV other than nicotine; no medical or psychiatric reaction to earlier MDMA. In the second phase everyone was phenotyped with dextromethorphan and classed as an extensive CYP2D6 metabolizer; the paper does not say separately whether the six pilot men were phenotyped (Methods, 1st and 3rd paragraphs).
sample.demographics: All men; mean age 26.5 years (range 21-31), weight 74.4 kg (66-83), height 178 cm (169-186). All but two were current smokers; average alcohol intake 2 units a day (1 unit = 8 g ethanol); all had previously used cannabis, cocaine and methamphetamine (Methods, 1st paragraph).
sample.attrition: None reported: all 14 are analysed; the second MDA value at 50 mg was below the quantification limit (Table 1 footnote).
sample.selection_effects: Men only, young, healthy, experienced with MDMA, and (in the second phase) all extensive CYP2D6 metabolizers; women, people with slow or intermediate CYP2D6 activity and people with liver or other disease were not studied. The 150 mg dose caused cardiovascular and subjective side effects in the volunteers who took it, which is why higher doses were not given (Results, 3rd paragraph), so the top of the dose range comes from two men who tolerated it.

exposure.measurement: MDMA given in the laboratory and measured directly: MDMA, MDA, HMMA and HMA in plasma (13 times to 24 hours) and urine (2 or 3 collection periods) by gas chromatography with nitrogen-specific detection, directly or after hydrolysis of glucuronide conjugates, by a method described in an earlier paper (Methods > Analytical methods).
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Study conditions only: single oral doses of racemic MDMA of 50, 75, 100, 125 and 150 mg; 75 and 125 mg were taken by the same eight men in randomized order, the other three doses by two different men each.
exposure.polysubstance: No other drug was given in the MDMA conditions; the amphetamine and placebo conditions of the crossover are not reported. The paper does not describe drug screening or abstinence rules before sessions.
exposure.abstinence_at_testing: Not described; the interval between crossover sessions is not stated in the paper.

comparison.controls: No placebo comparison is used for the pharmacokinetic analysis. The comparison is across dose levels: within person for 75 against 125 mg (n=8) and between persons for 50, 100 and 150 mg (n=2 each).
comparison.matching: Randomized Latin-square order for the second phase; no matching for the pilot volunteers.
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Not applicable to a pharmacokinetic comparison, except that the pilot and crossover men are different people whose enzyme activity and body size could differ at each dose.

outcomes.instruments: Plasma and urinary MDMA, MDA, HMMA and HMA; pharmacokinetic parameters (peak concentration, time to peak, area under the curve, half-life, total, renal and non-renal clearance); urinary recovery. Psychomotor performance, subjective effects, heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, pupil diameter and electrocardiogram were also measured in the second phase but only diastolic blood pressure at the peak time is reported, for five men (Methods; Results, 3rd paragraph; Fig. 3).
outcomes.validity_norms: The assay is cited to an earlier paper; precision and limits of quantification are not given here beyond the footnote that one MDA value was below the limit.
outcomes.operationalization: Non-linearity is judged from dose-normalized area under the curve (AUC divided by dose), from the recovery of unchanged MDMA and of HMMA in urine, and from the split of clearance into renal and non-renal parts; no dose-proportionality model is fitted.
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: None. Separate tests are reported: a paired t test of dose-normalized AUC(0-infinity) at 75 and 125 mg (P<0.03), a Kruskal-Wallis test across five doses (P<0.1), a bioequivalence interval, and analyses of variance of renal clearance (not significant) and non-renal clearance (P<0.03).
outcomes.assessor_blinding: The second phase is described as double-blind; the pilot phase is not described as blinded. Plasma assays are objective.

analysis.effect_sizes: Printed in Table 1 (mean and SD for n=8; two individual values for n=2): 75 mg, peak 130.9 (SD 38.6) ug/L, AUC(0-24 h) 1331.5 (646.0) ug.h/L, dose-normalized AUC 17.8 (8.6), half-life 7.7 (3.2) h, total clearance 86.9 (74.4) L/h; 125 mg, peak 236.4 (58.0), AUC 2623.7 (572.9), normalized AUC 21.0 (4.6), half-life 8.6 (3.2), total clearance 51.1 (14.1) L/h, non-renal clearance 38.1 L/h against 74.0 at 75 mg (the SDs are cut off in the image). Editors' calculation from the printed means: a 1.67-fold dose gave 1.81 times the peak and 1.97 times the AUC, which is 18% above proportionality on dose-normalized AUC. Only one interval is given: a 90% interval of -0.3 to 89.3% for the within-person ratio.
analysis.preregistration_detail: A trial authorized by the Spanish Ministry of Health (General Directorate of Pharmacy and Health Products, no. 95/297); no registry entry is mentioned. The authors call the non-linearity an unexpected observation made retrospectively.
analysis.selective_reporting: The second phase measured effects, psychomotor tests and cardiovascular variables and the amphetamine and placebo conditions, none of which is reported except diastolic pressure in five men. Table 2 and the text do not say how the five men for the HMMA re-analysis were chosen.
analysis.power: No sample-size reasoning. n=8 within person for 75 against 125 mg and n=2 for each of the other doses.

interpretation_gap.results_show: In eight extensive CYP2D6 metabolizers, 125 mg gave a peak concentration 1.8 times and an exposure 2.0 times those after 75 mg (a 1.67-fold dose; editors' calculation), non-renal clearance about halved (74.0 to 38.1 L/h), more unchanged MDMA in urine (71.2 to 169.6 micromol, 2.4-fold) and about the same total HMMA recovery. The two men at 150 mg had an exposure of about 5,100 and 5,200 ug.h/L, about twice the mean at 125 mg for a 1.2-fold dose, but each of the 50, 100 and 150 mg points rests on two men, and the two men at 50 mg differ 8-fold in exposure (100.1 and 813.9). The five-dose comparison was only marginally significant (P<0.1).
interpretation_gap.claimed: The abstract concludes that the lack of linearity is "a more general phenomenon" concerning the whole population independent of CYP2D6 genotype, and that small dose increases give disproportionate concentration rises so that people are more prone to acute toxicity. The main comparison was in extensive metabolizers only, so independence from genotype was not tested; no toxicity outcome was analysed; the observation was retrospective, from studies not designed for it; and the authors themselves say saturation of metabolism cannot be excluded and that the same people were not tested at every dose. The abstract's results sentence is worded with more care (concentrations that did not follow proportionality, which could be indicative of non-linearity).

timeline.event: Same group: a second 100 mg dose 24 hours after the first gave 77% higher exposure than the first dose (see the card for Farre et al.)

Narrative review by the same group on MDMA, methamphetamine and CYP2D6 pharmacogenetics: describes MDMA as an inactivator of its own main metabolizing enzyme, which this paper offers as one of two possible causes, and takes the share of clearance handled by that enzyme from this paper and a 2005 study
Same group: 50 mg two hours before 100 mg raised the peak concentration to 311 from 203 ng/mL, 12.8% above dose proportionality

Independent group: pooled analysis of 139 healthy people in which seven with no CYP2D6 function had a peak MDMA level 15% higher than people with normal function, in the first three hours only, which the authors read as MDMA blocking the enzyme in everyone

replication.where_it_stands: More-than-proportional exposure after a larger or a repeated dose has been seen again in controlled studies, mostly by this group (authors overlap with Farre et al. 2004) and in a booster design by another group, so the direction is supported; the size at a given dose, the role of genotype and the cause (self-inhibition against saturation) are not settled by this paper, which rests on eight men for the key comparison.

funding.funder: Grants FIS 97/1198, CIRIT (1997SGR00077), ISCIII 97/4344 and Plan Nacional sobre Drogas, Madrid; the Spanish Ministry of Health supplied the MDMA (Methods; Acknowledgments).
funding.declared_conflicts: Not reported: the article carries no conflict-of-interest statement.
funding.affiliations_note: Authors de la Torre, Farre, Ortuno, Roset and Cami also wrote Farre et al. (2004), so later repeated-dose studies from this group are not independent of this one. The page text does not give affiliations.

what_would_settle_it: A prospective study in which the same volunteers take at least four single doses in randomized, blinded order with washouts, including women and people with slow and intermediate CYP2D6 activity (genotyped and phenotyped), large enough to fit a dose-proportionality model with intervals, with an intravenous or a probe-drug measure of CYP2D6 activity after each dose to separate self-inhibition from saturation and absorption from clearance.

domains.note: In the second phase conditions were randomly assigned in a balanced Latin square, but sequence generation and allocation concealment are not described, and the pilot doses were not randomized; the comparison across five doses is between persons for three of them.
The Latin square balances order, but the washout between sessions is not stated.
Plasma and urine concentrations are objective and do not depend on the blind; no deviations are reported.

All 14 men are analysed, but plasma HMMA and blood pressure were re-analysed in one man per dose level (five men), selected without a stated rule, and one MDA value at 50 mg was below the limit of quantification.
Chromatographic assay for MDMA and metabolites with a published method; precision is not reported here.

An unplanned retrospective analysis of studies with other aims; the five-dose test is only P<0.1; the printed dose-normalized AUC(0-24 h) values cannot give the reported paired P<0.03 (see reporting issues); the pharmacodynamic data collected were not reported.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: The within-person randomized comparison of 75 and 125 mg gives a clear and plausible signal of more-than-proportional exposure with halved non-renal clearance, and the direction has been seen in later controlled studies. The overall judgment is set by the unplanned retrospective analysis, the dependence of the wider dose range on two men per dose, a statistical description with inconsistencies, and a Table 2 misprint. The source can be cited for more-than-proportional MDMA exposure between 75 and 125 mg in eight men who are extensive CYP2D6 metabolizers and for lower non-renal clearance at 125 mg; it cannot be cited for the shape of the curve from 50 to 150 mg, for genotype-independence, for women, for people with slower metabolism, or for toxicity.

key_findings.finding: Fourteen men took part: six in a pilot phase (two each at 50, 100 and 150 mg) and eight in a double-blind, randomized, Latin-square crossover of 75 mg MDMA, 125 mg MDMA, 40 mg amphetamine and placebo; all had used MDMA at least five times; in the second phase all were extensive CYP2D6 metabolizers. The 150 mg volunteers had side effects that ruled out higher doses, and 50 mg was judged low.
key_findings.locator: Methods > Patients and study design, 1st to 3rd paragraphs; Abstract (Methods)

key_findings.finding: In the same eight men, 125 mg gave a higher dose-normalized exposure than 75 mg: peak 236.4 ug/L (SD 58.0) against 130.9 (38.6); AUC(0-24 h) 2623.7 (572.9) against 1331.5 (646.0); dose-normalized AUC 21.0 (4.6) against 17.8 (8.6); half-life 8.6 (3.2) against 7.7 (3.2) h. A paired t test of dose-normalized AUC(0-infinity) gave P<0.03, and the 90% interval of the within-person ratio was -0.3 to 89.3%, so the authors judged the 125 mg dose not bioequivalent to the 75 mg dose scaled by dose. Editors' calculation: 1.67 times the dose gave 1.81 times the peak and 1.97 times the AUC.
key_findings.locator: Table 1 (image; MDMA rows for 75 and 125 mg); Results, 1st paragraph

key_findings.finding: Urinary clearance of MDMA was roughly constant across doses (analysis of variance not significant) while non-renal clearance depended on dose (P<0.03) and, in the same eight men, was about halved at 125 mg (38.1 L/h) against 75 mg (74.0 L/h), which the authors read as impaired hepatic clearance; total clearance was 86.9 (SD 74.4) against 51.1 (14.1) L/h. The SDs of non-renal clearance are cut off at the edge of the table image.

Across the five doses (50 to 150 mg, a 3-fold range) the AUC(0-24 h) of MDMA varied more than 10-fold: two men at 50 mg had 100.1 and 813.9 ug.h/L, two men at 150 mg 5132.8 and 5232.0, with peak concentrations 441.9 and 486.9 ug/L at 150 mg against a mean of 236.4 at 125 mg. A Kruskal-Wallis test of dose-normalized AUC(0-infinity) across the five doses was only marginal (P<0.1).
key_findings.locator: Table 1 (image; 50, 100 and 150 mg rows); Results, 1st paragraph; Discussion, 1st paragraph

key_findings.finding: About half the dose was recovered in urine in 24 hours at every dose (Table 2: 51.0 SD 16.2 and 53.7 SD 11.4 percent in the two groups of eight). Unchanged MDMA recovery rose from 71.2 (SD 13.7) micromol at 75 mg to 169.6 (69.5) at 125 mg (editors' calculation: 2.4-fold for a 1.67-fold dose), while HMMA recovery stayed in the same range (128.3, SD 21.8, then 148.3, SD 102.8 micromol). The authors take the roughly constant HMMA with rising MDMA to point to saturation or inhibition of the demethylenation step, and say unchanged MDMA recovery rose by a factor of nearly 20 across the dose range.

In five men, one per dose level, plasma HMMA exceeded MDMA at 50, 75 and 100 mg and the reverse held at the higher doses; diastolic blood pressure at the time of peak concentration followed MDMA's peak concentration, with a clear non-linearity at 150 mg. Figures 2 and 3 show single men and their values were not extracted.
key_findings.locator: Results, 3rd paragraph; Fig. 2 and Fig. 3 legends and images

key_findings.finding: The authors name two explanations: saturation of MDMA metabolism (the simplest, which they say cannot be excluded) and inhibition of CYP2D6-mediated demethylenation by MDMA, and perhaps by its metabolite HMMA; they cite in vitro work showing MDMA is both a substrate and an inhibitor of CYP2D6, with inhibition increasing after preincubation (up to 95% of control activity at 1.5 micromolar, as worded in the paper), at concentrations they say are compatible with those in the body.

Authors' stated limits: the observations were made retrospectively and the clinical studies were not designed to detect the phenomenon, so bias cannot be excluded from the fact that the same individuals were not tested at each dose level; they still say acute toxic effects reported after recreational doses should be read in the light of dose-dependent kinetics.

reporting_issues.issue: The image of Table 1 in the PMC copy is cut off at its right edge: the last column (non-renal clearance) shows 74.0 (71.1 and 38.1 (13.3 for the 75 and 125 mg groups, and the 50 mg range ends 734.1-56.5, with the closing digits missing.
reporting_issues.consequence: The standard deviations of the non-renal clearances on which the 'reduced by one half' statement rests cannot be read in this copy; their values were not extracted and should be checked in the journal's printed page.

reporting_issues.issue: Footnote 2 of Table 1 says the MDMA concentrations of the second volunteer were under the quantification limit, but it is attached to the MDA row at 50 mg (n=1) while MDMA values for both 50 mg men are printed (19.8-82.8 ug/L).
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor: MDA is evidently meant; the MDA values at 50 mg rest on one man.

reporting_issues.issue: In Table 2 the second man at 50 mg has MDMA 40.9, MDA 1.0, HMMA 89.2 and HMA 4.2 micromol, which sum to 135.3 micromol (52.2% of the 259 micromol dose), but the printed dose excreted for him is 38.3%. With 4.9 in place of 40.9 the sum is 99.3 micromol, which is 38.3%. Every other individual and group value reconciles with its printed percentage (editors' arithmetic). The text's 'factor of nearly 20' for MDMA recovery fits 4.9 (group means 12.8 against 246.8 micromol, 19.3-fold) and not 40.9 (30.8 against 246.8, 8.0-fold).
reporting_issues.consequence: A likely lost decimal point; the 50 mg urinary MDMA values should not be quoted, and the statement of a nearly 20-fold rise holds only if the value is 4.9.

reporting_issues.issue: The paired t test is reported as P<0.03 for dose-normalized AUC(0-infinity), a quantity not printed anywhere. The printed dose-normalized AUC(0-24 h) values (17.8, SD 8.6, and 21.0, SD 4.6, n=8 each) cannot give P<0.03 in a paired test at any within-person correlation: the smallest two-sided P that these means and SDs allow is about 0.06, at a correlation of 1 (editors' calculation).
reporting_issues.consequence: The significance claimed for the key within-person comparison cannot be checked from the paper; the more-than-proportional rise is better described by the ratio of means (1.97 times the AUC for 1.67 times the dose) than by the P value.

reporting_issues.issue: A Kruskal-Wallis test and an analysis of variance across the five dose levels treat 75 and 125 mg as independent groups although they are the same eight men (16 of the 22 observations).
reporting_issues.consequence: The assumptions of both tests are not met; the five-dose P values (P<0.1 and P<0.03) are not valid as stated.

reporting_issues.issue: The text calls the roughly constant HMMA recovery almost constant at around 100 micromol, but Table 2 shows individual HMMA recoveries from 59.8 to 152.0 micromol and a group SD of 102.8 micromol at 125 mg (mean 148.3, against 128.3 at 75 mg); no test of HMMA recovery against dose is given.
reporting_issues.consequence: The constant-HMMA part of the saturation argument describes group means with a wide spread and no statistical test.

reporting_issues.issue: Clearances are computed from oral doses, so they are dose divided by AUC and include bioavailability; the paper reads the fall in non-renal clearance as impaired hepatic clearance, yet also uses the words higher bioavailability for the 125 mg dose.
reporting_issues.consequence: Without an intravenous dose, a fall in clearance and a rise in absorption cannot be told apart; the finding should be quoted as more-than-proportional exposure, not as a mechanism.

reporting_issues.issue: The abstract says the non-linearity concerns the whole population independent of CYP2D6 genotype, but in the second phase everyone was an extensive metabolizer, and it says people are therefore more prone to acute toxicity although no toxicity outcome was analysed.
reporting_issues.consequence: Both statements go beyond the data; the paper supports a more-than-proportional rise in exposure in extensive metabolizers only.

verification.source_read: PMC full text PMC2014905 (all sections and the reference list read as text). Tables 1 and 2 and Figures 2 and 3 are images and were read on screen; the right-hand edge of the Table 1 image is cut off in the PMC copy.
